answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by tying each identity to a scarce, verifiable work history instead of free sign-up. Reputation works like a walnut: the shell only hardens layer by layer, so a newcomer must first do useful, publicly witnessed work before its votes count — say, writing a sonnet of benchmark proofs that established peers attest. Creating a thousand fakes then costs the attacker real effort each time, the way extracting copper costs energy no one can fake. Voting weight grows from demonstrated work, not from self-made claims.
